title: OAuth 2.0
subtitle: I built an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for commercial AI assistants, with consent as the real control, and my memory gateway validates tokens from several issuers against published keys.

stats.label: a newly registered client waits for a person's approval before it lapses

lede: Auth and access plane exists because I wanted commercial AI assistants to reach my private tool estate through standard OAuth, with a person approving every grant. I built the authorization server. It implements the authorization-code grant with PKCE, with the S256 check written from primitives, plus client credentials, refresh tokens and revocation, with separate authentication paths for confidential and public clients. Tokens are RS256-signed JWTs. The signing key persists, so tokens survive restarts, and the public keys are published for every verifier. Assistants find the server through authorization-server and protected-resource metadata, register through dynamic client registration and name the resource they want, with a default when they do not.
quote: The consent screen is the control point, so open registration works with every assistant and no token is issued without a person's approval.
evidence: OAuth 2.0 and identity architecture: an authorization server with the authorization-code grant and PKCE, an S256 check written from primitives, client credentials, refresh tokens, revocation and RS256-signed JWTs.

Dynamic client registration and consent design: discovery metadata and open registration for AI assistants, a pending client lapsing after 30 days without a person's approval, and no token issued without it.
Zero-trust architecture: a protected MCP resource that introspects every bearer token on every request and refuses, with no cached allow, when introspection cannot answer.

Delegated authorization for AI agents: offline multi-issuer token validation with a scope tree and one-time-code step-up, sub-agent tokens that end with their parent, and atomic refresh so no refresh token is spent twice.
author: Corey James
